newsitem.title: USA: US corp bonds close up, telecoms dominate trade.
newsitem.headline: US corp bonds close up, telecoms dominate trade.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds regained footing with U.S. Treasuries to close higher, while high-yield activity was dominated by telecom debt in the wake of Monday's MFS Communications/WorldCom merger, traders said.
Junk trading was also punctuated by volatile markets in Grand Casino's Inc debt, traders said.

In the telecom sector, Teleport Communications Group debt closed about one point higher in active trade, dealers said. The 9.875 percent senior notes due 2006 were quoted at 100-1/2 bid, 101 offer and the zero coupon senior discount notes due 2007 were quoted at 61-1/8 bid, 61-5/8 offer.
Telewest Communications zero coupon debt closed at 61-3/4 bid, 62-1/4 offer, up about 1/2 point from Monday's close, one trader said.

MFS Communications 8-7/8 percent debt due 2006 slipped about 1/2 point to 68 bid to 68-1/2 offer. The MFS debt jumped roughly five points following news that WorldCom Inc would acquire the company in a stock swap worth about $14 million, creating a giant international business communications firm.
"This merger has a the street assessing value all over the place," one trader said. "That got a lot moving today, a lot for the week before Labor Day, anyway."
Elsewhere, junk-rated Grand Casinos Inc notes rose in volatile trade, dealers said.
Sent into a spin on news of a surprisingly large charge against future earnings, Grand Casinos' 10-1/8 percent first mortgage notes closed unchanged at 97-1/4 bid, 97-3/4 offer.
The notes were actively trading throughout the session in a 96-1/2 to 97-1/2 range, one trader said.
Grand said on Tuesday it expects to record a non-cash charge of $0.55 to $0.60 in the second half of fiscal 1996 as a result of operating losses at Stratosphere Corp.
Grand said the charge is about $0.50 per share higher than originally estimated. Grand Casinos owns about 42 percent of Stratosphere.
Grand Casino stock gained 1-3/8 to close at 17-3/8.
The broad market was quoted unchanged to up 1/4 point.

Turning to investment grade trade, dealers said secondary action took a back seat to a double-dose of new banking sector paper. Although trade was thin, quotes for high-grade bonds firmed as technical buying lifted U.S. Treasuries.
The 30-year Treasury bond ended up 10/32 at 97-6/32 to yield 6.97 percent. The bond closed at 7.00 percent on Monday.
In the new issue market, Swiss Bank Corp issued a total of $450 million in two-parts via lead managers Swiss Bank and Merrill Lynch & Co Inc.

The first tranche included $150 million 10-year subordinated notes priced to yield 7.30 percent, or 53 basis points over the 10-year U.S. Treasury note. Another $300 million 30-year subordinated notes were priced to yield 7.784 percent, or 77 basis points over the 30-year Treasury bond.
Price talk early in the session called for spreads of 50 basis points for the 10-year tranche and 70 basis points for the 30-year tranche.
The entire issue is rated AA2/AA and is non-callable.
Elsewhere, KeyCorp unit Key Bank issued $165 million subordinated bank notes due 2008 to yield 7.516 percent, or a spread of 75 basis points over the Treasury curve.
Salomon Brothers acted as lead manager on the deal.
The deal is non-callable and rated A1/A-minus.
